text:
Cheng: Quick sanity check — during int8/AWQ bring-up for gpt-13b-v2 we see ~1.8% ROUGE-L delta on summarization with prefetch + continuous batching enabled. Prefetch off -> delta disappears. Anyone seen similar? I'm running with kv_cache_prefetch=true, cont_batch_ms=12.

Anya: Can you paste the exact config + eval command?

Cheng: Config and eval below:
```
model: gpt-13b-v2-awq-int8
kv_cache_prefetch: true
cont_batch_ms: 12
max_batch_tokens: 2048
quant: awq
```
Eval: python eval.py --dataset news-sum --split val --n=200 --seed 42

Miguel: Which quant backend/build? AWQ on CUDA or CPU fallback? Also which kernel variant (f32 accum vs int8 accum)?

Cheng: AWQ on CUDA (cu117), using our awq-kernel build (awq-v2-opt). Tried GPTQ variant as a control — GPTQ shows FP32-like quality. The weird delta only shows for AWQ when prefetch is on.

Lina: My first guess: prefix cache may return slightly stale KV pairs if continuous batching reorders requests. Staleness + small tokenization differences can push generation into a different beam path.

Evan: We have a repro harness for ordering issues. Can you enable tracing headers and PREFETCH tracing? Try env TRACE_PREFETCH=1 and PREFETCH_TIMEOUT_MS=0 to force immediate behavior so we can see timing.

Cheng: Added traces. Sample log snippet:
```
[2026-03-18 12:02:31] PREFETCH hit: key=abc123 seq=1 ts=1700244151 stale=false
[2026-03-18 12:02:31] PREFETCH hit: key=abc124 seq=1 ts=1700244152 stale=true
```
The samples marked stale=true map to the eval cases where ROUGE drops.

Anya: If cont-batching groups queries with different prefixes, prefetch could evict or overwrite cache entries in-flight. Try disabling continuous batching or increase cache TTL and see if numbers recover.

Miguel: Also double-check batch ordering: our cont-batcher can merge requests that start within cont_batch_ms window and then interleave cache fills. Filing runtime task to add sequence checks.

ops-bot: Deployed canary: model=gpt-13b-v2-awq-int8 region=us-west-2 canary_id=c-422 cont_batch_ms=40 kv_cache_prefetch=true (rollout=canary).

Lina: If the canary confirms the regression disappears when cont_batch_ms is larger, we should add a guard in the runtime to disable prefetch when cont_batch_ms < 20 or set a safe TTL.

Cheng: I'll run a small sweep this afternoon: prefetch on/off, cont_batch_ms=[0,12,40], cache_ttl=[50,500], n=200 samples each. Will post the numbers here. Thanks for the quick eyes! :thumbsup:

Anya: Thanks — if you can attach the eval diffs (diffed outputs and token-level alignments) that will help root cause.

Cheng: Will do, uploading artifacts to /mnt/evals/1845123456/sweep.tar.gz when done.
